_what_this_is: The machine-readable requirement declaration for a catalog entity.
catalog.py reads this file and validates every entity against it.
STANDARDS.md points at this file rather than restating it, so prose
cannot drift away from what the validator actually enforces.
This is deliberately NOT JSON Schema. jsonschema is not installed in
this environment and must not be vendored: the requirement is a flat
list of parameters with four attributes each, a hand-rolled validator
for it is about 120 lines and a reader can audit it in one sitting,
and a draft-07 interpreter is neither.

confidence_vocabulary.published: Vendor specification sheet or official manual. Cite the page.
confidence_vocabulary.derived: Computed from published values. State the computation in 'note'.
confidence_vocabulary.literature: Peer-reviewed paper or engineering textbook typical value.
confidence_vocabulary.estimated: Engineering judgement. State the basis and tolerance in 'note'.

parameter_statuses.present: Default when 'status' is absent. 'value' must be non-null, 'confidence' must be from the vocabulary, and 'source' is mandatory.
parameter_statuses.missing: A declared gap. 'value' MUST be null, 'confidence' MUST be absent, and a 'todo' string is mandatory.
parameter_statuses.not_applicable: Does not apply to this airframe. 'value' MUST be null, 'confidence' MUST be absent, and 'note' must explain why.
parameter_statuses._absent_key: A parameter key that is not in the file at all is NOT RECORDED. For completeness scoring it counts the same as 'missing', but it is reported differently: an author who wrote status 'missing' with a todo has demonstrably looked, and one who omitted the key has not.

requirement_classes.REQUIRED_MEASURED: Must be present AND carry confidence 'published' or 'derived'. These are the parameters the model is most sensitive to; a guess in any one of them invalidates every number downstream, regardless of how well sourced the rest of the record is.
requirement_classes.REQUIRED_MODELING: Must be present. 'literature' and 'estimated' are acceptable, because these are modelling choices rather than facts about the aircraft, but 'source' is still mandatory so the choice is auditable.
requirement_classes.REQUIRED_FOR_OPERATIONAL: Must be present only when the operational profile is used. An entity missing these can still produce spec-profile figures while being structurally incapable of producing an operational planning number.
requirement_classes.OPTIONAL: Recorded when known. Absence never blocks modelling, but anchors listed in the entity's own calibration block are checked separately by a cross-field rule.

R0.name: STUB
R0.meaning: Below R1. The gate REFUSES. No number can be produced, because a required input is absent.

R1.name: PROVISIONAL
R1.meaning: No schema errors and every REQUIRED_MEASURED and REQUIRED_MODELING parameter present. The model runs and every output carries a PROVISIONAL banner.

R2.name: MODELED
R2.meaning: R1, plus every REQUIRED_MEASURED parameter is published or derived, every present parameter carries a source, nothing is dated in the future, and the calibration block is internally coherent. Output is unstamped.

R3.name: VALIDATED
R3.meaning: R2, plus at least two held-out anchors present and scorable, REQUIRED_FOR_OPERATIONAL complete, and the oldest verified_on within the staleness limit. Quotable as a planning product. A held-out anchor that MISSES does not block R3 so long as the miss is scored and on the record - see STANDARDS.md section 8.

the calibration anchor; the one parameter that is fitted is fitted to this
parasitic power; negligible at hover, matters in cruise

cross_field_rules: filename_matches_entity_id: the file basename without extension must equal entity_id. Catches the commonest stub-authoring error - copy an existing entity, rename the file, forget the id inside.
calibration_block_present: 'calibration' must exist with fitted_parameter, fitted_to_anchor and held_out_anchors.
calibration_anchors_exist: every anchor named by fitted_to_anchor or held_out_anchors must exist as a parameter in performance_published.
fitted_anchor_not_held_out: fitted_to_anchor must not also appear in held_out_anchors. An anchor cannot both set a parameter and test it.

verified_on_not_future: no verified_on may be more than one day in the future. A verification date that has not happened yet is a data-entry fault, and treating it as fresh errs in the wrong direction.
status_field_coherence: see parameter_statuses. A number under status 'missing', or a null under status 'present', is an error.
